title: 2023 draft budget review and requested changes
subtitle: Deferred requests on traffic calming, health care recruitment and business licensing; downtown garbage, BID budgets, Black History Month funding.
overview: The Committee of the Whole spent the day on the 2023 draft budget. Staff presented a Township levy increase of 3.48%, about $45 more on an average assessed home, and said inflation and growth made it a difficult budget to prepare. After hearing delegations and working through a list of requested changes, the committee recommended the 2023 budget {{vote:m15}}. The Fergus BIA budget was voted on separately because of a declared conflict {{vote:m14}}.

Many requests were deferred rather than funded now. The committee recommended deferring a larger transfer to the General Capital Reserve to 2024 budget deliberations {{vote:m5}}, and asked for staff reports on traffic calming {{vote:m6}} and health care recruitment {{vote:m9}}. A business licensing review was put off until after strategic planning {{vote:m8}}. The minutes also record a motion to extend the co-op position in the CAO's office.

The committee also recommended a public consultation approach to budgeting ahead of the 2023 process {{vote:m11}}, downtown garbage talks with Wellington County {{vote:m10}}, and $3,000 for Black History Month events {{vote:m12}}. These recommendations go to Council for adoption.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the 2023 Budget, which staff had presented with a Township levy increase of 3.48%.
The committee recommended deferring an increase to the General Capital Reserve, as outlined in the asset management plan, to the 2024 Budget deliberations.
The committee recommended deferring any increase to the traffic calming budget to a staff report in April 2023.
The committee recommended deferring discussion of a business licensing review capital project until after the Strategic Planning process.
The committee recommended deferring assistance with health care professional recruitment to a staff report in February 2023.
The committee recommended that staff and the Mayor start garbage collection talks about the downtown cores with Wellington County.
The committee recommended a public consultation and engagement approach to budgeting ahead of the 2023 budget process.
The committee recommended $3000 for the CW Black Committee, funded from the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Implementation capital project.

debate: Staff said the 3.48% increase was reached after cutting about 2.27 percentage points from an initial request. Cuts included the asset management reserve increase, and staff cautioned that inflation was estimated to add 9.1% to the cost of delivering the same services.

Delegates from the Fergus and Elora BIAs described downtown garbage collection as a growing problem, partly from residential tenants above businesses. One said the Fergus BIA now pays for private pickup. Councillors asked who the extra service is meant to serve and whether the Township could raise the issue with the County.

A hospital delegate said recruiting and housing visiting hospitalists and emergency physicians is costing more, and that funding needs will likely rise above the usual $20,000. Councillors asked what the money would cover, and staff said a fuller report would come back.

A resident delegate urged an advisory finance committee, tighter staffing growth and reconsidering the operations facility. Staff defended the staffing strategy as lean and driven by growth and legislation. A councillor said the County may be open to sharing the operations facility.

Councillors discussed adding CAO office support, restoring the asset management contribution and increasing traffic calming. Staff asked that changes be held on a list and decided together later in the process.
